sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Somewhat unusual within the genus. The worker is small, and the odd primary cushion (PC) has no crest but bears strong setae where the crest would be, so that the worker is easily confused with species of Ternicubitermes (bilobatodes type of enteric valve architecture, EVA) and of Cubitermes (sensu Hellemans et al. 2021); it can be separated from them because the fore coxa is ridged and bears 3–4 strong spines (the fore coxa of Ternicubitermes and Cubitermes workers is an unarmed cone). The odd primary cushion has few supporting setae, 5–10 on each side; odd primary cushion elongation index WVPOdd-Elg = 9.79–13.6. The soldier is small within the genus, with very weakly curved mandibles (weaker than in I. rectimalatus), the left mandible minor curvature SMlc = 0.11–0.16 mm. The alate is medium-sized within the genus and almost impossible to distinguish from I. severus and I. ugandensis ugandensis, the ocelli being larger than in I. ugandensis (IOcD = 0.20–0.22 mm). It is at present known only from Angola.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark (C6), the frontal gland pore one shade paler; postclypeus concolorous with the head capsule; antennae C4–C5. Pronotum concolorous with the head capsule, meso- and metanotum C4, slightly paler than the head; tibiae C5, slightly paler than the femora C4. Abdominal tergites C5; sternites distinctly paler in the middle (C3) and darker at the sides (C5), the posterior sternites (C4–C5) darker than the anterior ones. Head capsule with conspicuous setae scattered over a dense felt of short fine hairs; labrum and postclypeus with conspicuous setae mixed with short hairs; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, most segments with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at the tip (visible above 50×). Pronotum setae mainly on the margins, shorter in the middle; meso- and metanotum with fine pale hairs arranged along the median band, the posterior lobe also with large setae; legs hairy, the fore coxa with 9–10 stronger setae on the ridge and 3–4 ventrally, the trochanter with 8–9; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, each tibia with 15–30 spines. Abdominal tergites with setae of mixed sizes; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward, together with many small setae directed posteriorly. Compound eyes short-oval; ocelli relatively large (IOcD > 0.20 mm), oval, separated from the compound eye by about 0.8–0.9 times the small ocellar diameter; frontal gland pore generally a small circular or elongate mark. Antennae 16-segmented (the queen 13-segmented through damage). Labrum domed, wider than long. Left mandible apical tooth small within the genus, more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 3 marginal teeth, but the second expressed only as an undulation of the tooth margin between the first and third; only the apical tooth sharp in unworn specimens; the premolar unobstructed and clearly visible in dorsal view; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded molar prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible apical tooth always more prominent than the first marginal tooth, with 2 marginal teeth, the second blunt-tipped even in fresh specimens; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum distinctly wider than long, narrower than the head width (including compound eyes), flat to very weakly saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe short and very slightly raised. The fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Gut not studied. Measurements: compound eye major diameter 0.42–0.46 mm, head width including compound eyes 1.69–1.71 mm, ocellus major diameter 0.20–0.22 mm, postclypeus width 0.83–0.85 mm, maximum pronotum width 1.37–1.43 mm, hind tibia length 1.84–2.02 mm, fore wing length 17.2 mm (n = 1).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule C4–C6; antennae and labrum concolorous with the head capsule or slightly paler; mandibles dark (C6–C8), the base abruptly paler (two shades), generally concolorous with the frons; thorax and legs paler than the head capsule (C2–C4); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Head capsule with scattered setae, a dense tuft of setae on the frons surrounding and hanging over the frontal gland pore; the labrum with 4–5 large setae on each lobe; pronotum and mesonotum with few setae, mainly on the margins; fore coxa with 2–6 spines or strong setae on the ridge and no spines ventrally, the trochanter generally with several strong setae in a row; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively (the latter sometimes weak), each tibia with 6–15 spines. Head capsule distinctly sclerotized, distinctly longer than wide; in dorsal view the sides mostly nearly parallel, very slightly narrowing in the posterior third to quarter, converging from the antennal sockets towards the mandible bases, the posterior margin regularly convex; the upper margin slightly to strongly concave, the angle between the mandibles and the frons obtuse, the frons with a small swelling hanging over the frontal gland pore; in ventral view the gulamentum narrowing in the posterior half, the anterior half rounded at the sides and extending into angular ear-like projections. Antennae 14–15 segmented. Labrum deeply bifurcate and wider than long, the sides nearly straight, the lobes rounded and without semitransparent tips, the anterior margin concave. Mandibles sabre-like, the inner margin smooth, each with 1 distinct but small marginal tooth near the molar area; mandibles distinctly shorter than the head, the surface smooth and shining; curvature very weak, among the weakest in the genus, the right mandible slightly more curved than the left. Pronotum saddle-shaped, 52%–56% of the head width, the anterior and posterior margins straight. The fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Gut: enteric valve inserted on the left side, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen; caecum small, visible in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, with 3–4 lobes; enteric valve primary cushions arranged with trigonal symmetry, the odd cushion narrow and longer than the even ones (muneris type of enteric valve architecture). Measurements: head length (to the anterior margin of the labrum) 2.44–2.59 mm, head width 1.78–1.94 mm, head dorsal concavity sagitta SHdC 0.04–0.08 mm, left mandible ventral length 2.15–2.22 mm, hind tibia length 1.50–1.62 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale (C2–C3); proximal antennal segments pale (C2), the apical segment two shades darker (C4); thorax, tergites and legs pale (C2–C3); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Head capsule and postclypeus with scattered erect setae; labrum with a few stout setae; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at its tip. Thoracic tergites with scattered setae; fore coxa ridged, with 1 fine seta, 3–4 spines on the ridge and 1–3 ventrally; fore trochanter with 6 spines in a row; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, each tibia with 7–15 spines. Abdominal tergites with scattered setae; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward, often pigmented, and with small setae directed posteriorly. Medium-sized. Head capsule weakly sclerotized (except the mandibles). Antennae 14–14.5 segmented. Labrum domed. Left mandible apical tooth well developed but shorter than in most species; 3 marginal teeth, the first well developed but blunt-tipped, the second weak (expressed only as an undulating tooth margin, disappearing with wear), the third blunt-tipped; the premolar unobstructed and clearly visible in dorsal view; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded molar prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible apical tooth well developed, sharp-tipped when fresh; 2 marginal teeth, the first well developed and sharp when fresh, the second smaller and blunt-tipped even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum saddle-shaped, about 63% of the head width. The fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Gut: enteric valve inserted on the left side, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Enteric valve primary cushions of the muneris type, with trigonal symmetry: the odd cushion narrow in its downstream part and bearing strong curved setae; supporting setae few, 5–10 on each side of the odd cushion; secondary cushions (SC) broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed. Caecum small, visible in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, with 3–4 small lobes. Measurements: maximum head width 1.16–1.29 mm, left mandible functional length 0.53–0.58 mm, distance from the left mandible apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.13–0.17 mm, hind tibia length 1.22–1.31 mm, odd primary cushion elongation index 9.79–13.6.

note: Adapted from the genus revision in Josens et al. (2025), original in English; measurements from Table 2 and the text of the original; distribution, hosts, DNA and figure numbers are not translated.
